avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inducer reduces ixazomib plasma concentrations and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; do not use concurrently with ixazomib

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate anticoagulant effects and increase bleeding risk with concurrent thrombocytopenia from ixazomib
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or limit to <400 IU daily; monitor for bleeding signs

caution_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effects may compound thrombocytopenia risk associated with ixazomib therapy
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor platelet counts and bleeding signs

caution_supplements.name: Garlic supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet properties may increase bleeding risk in combination with ixazomib-induced thrombocytopenia
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased bruising or bleeding; consider dose reduction if used

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly reduce ixazomib absorption; manufacturer recommends fasting or light meal
caution_foods.action: Take ixazomib on an empty stomach or with light meal; avoid heavy fatty foods

monitoring_notes: Monitor CBC closely for thrombocytopenia and peripheral neuropathy development during therapy. Assess for bleeding manifestations if supplements with antiplatelet properties are used concurrently.
